messages.subject: Backtransforming and predictions
parts:
Hello everyone, I need some assistance please with the back tranformation of my results. I´ve been working with this selected model
> summary(fm80)

Call:
occu(formula = ~1 ~ DAPROT + DFAGUA + DCENPOB + FELINO, data = umf)

Occupancy (logit-scale):
            Estimate   SE      z P(>|z|)
(Intercept)    -25.1 27.1 -0.925   0.355
DAPROT          21.0 23.0  0.915   0.360
DFAGUA         -40.9 44.9 -0.911   0.362
DCENPOB        -24.5 30.1 -0.814   0.415
FELINO          17.3 22.4  0.769   0.442

Detection (logit-scale):
 Estimate    SE     z P(>|z|)
    -1.31 0.463 -2.84 0.00455

AIC: 41.22389 
Number of sites: 36
ID of sites removed due to NA: 1 5 6 17 23 42 43
optim convergence code: 1
optim iterations: 108 
Bootstrap iterations: 0 

The next logical step is to transform the data with the backtransform and linnearComb functions but can't seem to get my code right, I tried two ways, but it doesn't work and the prediction is always the same.

Warning message:
In .local(object, ...) :
  Model did not converge. Try providing starting values or increasing maxit control argment.
> btf80<-backTransform(linearComb(fm80, coefficients = c(1), type = 'det'))
> btf80<-backTransform(linearComb(fm80, coefficients = c(1,0,0,0,0), type = 'det'))
Error in .local(obj, coefficients, ...) : 
  ncol(coefficients) == length(obj@estimates) is not TRUE
> 

Can someone please point me in the right direction? what am I doing wrong here?

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: Backtransforming and predictions
parts:
Hi Laura,

I think there are two issues. First, when doing backtransform/linearComb, your first command works because you are providing one coefficient value (i.e., for the intercept) for type='det', which matches because your detection model in fm80 is intercept-only. For your second linearComb command, you are providing 5 values in your coefficients argument but type is still 'det'. Maybe you mean for argument type to be 'state' instead, since your occupancy model has an intercept + 4 covariates?

More importantly though, your selected model fm80 did not converge (as unmarked has warned), and your parameter estimates are very large and very uncertain. I would not trust any inference/prediction from the model and suggest exploring why your model isn't converging, perhaps starting by trying to fit a simpler occupancy model (maybe intercept-only) and working your way back up to the more complex models.

Ken

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Backtransforming and predictions
parts:
Lack of convergence issues much of the time requires looking at the data rather just the output to figure out what's going on.  If you're willing to share the data, then more targeted help can be found.

If you don't want to or can't share the data with everyone on the list, that is very understandable.  Sharing an appropriate subset of the data might alleviate some concerns but if lack of convergence is an issue, then usually all of the data is needed.

If you're willing to share the data just certain with individuals, then all folks that I know on this list abide by the same rules:  (1) we share your data with no one else and (2) any responses once the data is shared with an individual just goes to you and not the list.  If you want to share any of those responses, then that's up to you.  However, you sharing good responses is certainly encouraged.

I'd be happy to look at the data and let you know what I see.

I'd also echo what Ken Kellner wrote.  The convergence issue should be fixed first.  (While the standard errors are on the same order as the estimates, it just might be that none of the variables have much effect given the others in the model and maybe some of the predictor variables are highly correlated with each other.  Again, it's hard to say without the data.)

The second issue would be stating in words what you want rather than just giving the code.  For example, do you want to make predictions of occupancy probabilities given specific values of the predictor variables? Do you want odds ratios?

Jim
